references.text: Both texts are about bringing difficult legal cases before the priests and judges for a decision.
Refers to the priest and the judge as those who stand in the presence of the Lord and pronounce judgment.
The context concerns two witnesses who must appear in a legal case, directly linked to verse 17.
Jehoshaphat appointed Levites, priests, and family heads to serve as judges in Jerusalem, in accordance with the principle of standing in the presence of the Lord.
The principle of bringing legal cases before God and judges.
Cases are to be brought before God for a decision between two parties.
Refers to the witness principle from the Mosaic Law requiring two or three witnesses.
Jesus cites the principle of two or three witnesses in connection with church discipline.
